messages.body_plain:
I want to create a list object, lets call it X_List, that gets appended every time a particular actionButton is pressed but I also want to put an upper limit on the number of elements that can be stored in X_List by deleting the oldest element whenever necessary to make room.

The values stored in each element of X_List will be lists, lets call them i_list, and their components will be:
- non-reactive versions of a few reactive variables
- a data.frame that should only get created when the actionButton is pressed.

I have no trouble creating i_list with the following code:

G_Set = reactive({
    set_name = input$GeneSetName
    Hugo = rownames(AggGenes())
    Entrez = gene_lookup[gene_lookup$Gene %in% Hugo,"Entrez"]
    G = list("Name" = set_name, "Hugo" = Hugo, "Entrez" = Entrez)
  })

  i_list = eventReactive(input$SaveGeneSet, {
    fpkm_dat = as.matrix(fpkm_dat)
    # Retrieve gene list from G_Set()
    genelist = G_Set()$Entrez
    genelist = list(genelist)
    # Run GSVA
    scores <- gsva(fpkm_dat,genelist,method="ssgsea",rnaseq=T)
    out_dat = G_Set()
    out_dat$GSVA = scores
    return(out_dat)
  })

I'm thinking I probably need to do one of the following:
- make X_List another eventReactive() object that is dependent on input$SaveGeneSet
- make X_List a reactiveValues() object and use observeEvent() to append it with an if statement to control its size
- make X_List a static environment variable and update it using observeEvent()

But I haven't been able to make any of these strategies work so I'm wondering if I'm just approaching this the wrong way.

messages.body_plain:
Sorry, I forgot to edit out the reactiveVal() part. If you use shiny = TRUE, you really don't need that anymore, since your counter will already behave reactively. Here's what the shiny app should look like:

ui <- fluidPage(
  actionButton("minus", "-1"),
  actionButton("plus", "+1"),
  textOutput("value")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {

  count <- counter$new(shiny = TRUE)

  observeEvent(input$minus, { count$setDecrement() })
  observeEvent(input$plus,  { count$setIncrement() })

  output$value <- renderText({ count$getValue() })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)

On Tuesday, August 1, 2017 at 10:00:07 PM UTC+1, Bárbara Borges wrote:
> Great question! The problem here is that Shiny has no way of knowing the object has changed. The best way to solve this is by introducing reactivity into the object class itself. This isn't at all obvious and what I'd recommend involves using a custom function that will likely make it to Shiny (or a related utilities packages). For now, though you just have to define it yourself:
>
> reactiveTrigger <- function() {
>   rv <- reactiveValues(a = 0)
>   list(
>     depend = function() {
>       rv$a
>       invisible()
>     },
>     trigger = function() {
>       rv$a <- isolate(rv$a + 1)
>     }
>   )
> }
>
>
> Let's unpack this. This construct allows you to create a reactive trigger that "knows" (though you have to tell it) when your object has changed (i.e. when it should "fire"/trigger) and when it should be aware of these changes (i.e. when you want it to update if somewhere else it fires). You can think of this construct as "baking reactivity" into your object. In order to keep your object usable outside of Shiny (if that's what you want), you can do a conditional based on a user-supplied parameter.
>
> I adapted your example to use this (and still be generic enough):
>
> library(shiny)
>
> reactiveTrigger <- function() {
>   rv <- reactiveValues(a = 0)
>   list(
>     depend = function() {
>       rv$a
>       invisible()
>     },
>     trigger = function() {
>       rv$a <- isolate(rv$a + 1)
>     }
>   )
> }
>
> counter <- R6::R6Class(
>   public = list(
>     initialize = function(shiny = FALSE) {
>       private$shiny = shiny
>       private$value = 0
>       private$rxTrigger = reactiveTrigger()
>     },
>     setIncrement = function() {
>       if (private$shiny) private$rxTrigger$trigger()
>       private$value = private$value + 1
>     },
>     setDecrement = function() {
>       if (private$shiny) private$rxTrigger$trigger()
>       private$value = private$value -1
>     },
>     getValue = function() {
>       if (private$shiny) private$rxTrigger$depend()
>       return(private$value)
>     }
>   ),
>   private = list(
>     shiny = NULL,
>     value = NULL,
>     rxTrigger = NULL
>   )
> )
>
> ui <- fluidPage(
>   actionButton("minus", "-1"),
>   actionButton("plus", "+1"),
>   textOutput("value")
> )
>
> server <- function(input, output, session) {
>   count <- reactiveVal(counter$new(shiny = TRUE))
>
>   observeEvent(input$minus, { count()$setDecrement() })
>   observeEvent(input$plus,  { count()$setIncrement() })
>
>   output$value <- renderText({ count()$getValue() })
> }
>
> shinyApp(ui, server)
>
>
> In order to be extra obvious about which object methods should call rxTrigger$trigger() and which ones shuold call rxTrigger$depend(), all of the function are prefixed by "set" by they change private$value and by "get" if they read private$value.
>
> Let me know if you have questions,
> Barbara
>
> On Sunday, July 30, 2017 at 8:55:36 PM UTC+1, Charlotte S wrote:
> > Dear shiny users :)
> >
> > I am trying to implement an app that use an object as a reactive value.
> > When attributes inside the object are changed, the UI should be notified and redraw.
> > This does not work. It seems that if I make a class object reactive, it does not notice changes on the attributes.
> > Is this true? If so, how can I make the reactive object react to changes in the attributes. In the following I have created a small example that illustrates my issue
> >
> > Thanks a lot for your help :)
> >
> > if (interactive()) {
> >
> >   counter <- R6Class(
> >     public  = list(value = 0,
> >          increase = function(){
> >            self$value = self$value + 1
> >          },
> >          decrease = function(){
> >            self$value = self$value -1
> >          },
> >          getValue = function(){
> >            return(self$value)
> >          }
> >   )
> > )
> >
> >   ui <- fluidPage(
> >     actionButton("minus", "-1"),
> >     actionButton("plus", "+1"),
> >     br(),
> >     textOutput("value")
> >   )
> >
> >
> >   # The comments below show the equivalent logic using reactiveValues()
> >   server <- function(input, output, session) {
> >
> >     c <- reactiveVal()
> >
> >     c(counter$new())
> >
> >     observeEvent(input$minus, {
> >       c()$decrease()
> >     })
> >
> >     observeEvent(input$plus, {
> >       c()$increase()
> >     })
> >
> >     output$value <- renderText({
> >       print(c()$getValue())
> >       # print(c()$value)
> >     })
> >   }
> >
> >   shinyApp(ui, server)
> >
> > }
> >
> >

messages.subject: Re: javascript not working in a Shiny module
messages.subject_clean: javascript not working in a Shiny module
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

You are correct that this is a namespace issue.

When you use Shiny.onInputChange("select_button") it triggers input$select_button in a regular app but in a module this will not work. Only inputs with that modules prefix will be accessible in the inputs for that module's server function.

So if you replace "select_button" with ns("select_button") it will work.

Kind Regards

Hi Joe,

You don't need to do that at all. Here's what CharOption should look like:

CharOption <- function(input, output, session, PODData, category) {

  cnamelist <- function(PODData,category) {

    PODData[PODData$Feature == category,]$Characteristic
  }

  updateSelectInput(session, "charact", choices = cnamelist(PODData,category))

  return(list(
    Charact = reactive({input$charact})
  ))
}

messages.subject: Is there any syntactic sugar for using debounce/throttle on an input value?
messages.subject_clean: Is there any syntactic sugar for using debounce/throttle on an input value?
messages.body_plain:
Suppose I have a numeric input with ID "num" and in the server I want to refer to `input$num`. I want it to fire no more than once every second, so I want to use the `throttle(r, 1000)` function.

This is the code I would:

num <- reactive(input$num)
num_t <- throttle(num, 1000)
observe({
  cat(num_t())
})

I was wondering if there's a more compact way to do this, without having to define a variable that only gets used in one place?

A bit more on this issue of javascript in Modules. It is curious to me that the ns comes into play at all in this case since all of the javascript functionality is occurring WITHIN the Module. Anyway, Carl has hit on something here as, though I was not able to get ns("select_button") to work, I can get this to work if I hard-code the name space id. For example, if I am using the name space id of "demo", then the following code does provide the desired functionality:

mutate(Delete = shinyInput(actionButton, nrow(insectData()), '', label = "Delete", onclick = 'Shiny.onInputChange("demo-select_button",  this.id <http://this.id>)'))

That is a huge step forward, but obviously it is counter to the point to have to hard-code the ns id into Module functions. I am still not sure why Carl's excellent suggestion of adding ns("select_button") (e.g., below) did not work but if anyone has insight on where I am going wrong with my syntax your comments would be appreciated.

mutate(Delete = shinyInput(actionButton, nrow(insectData()), '', label = "Delete", onclick = 'Shiny.onInputChange(ns("select_button"),  this.id <http://this.id>)'))

Thanks!

When you call callModule(CharOption, ...), don't pass category = results2(). Instead, do category = results2, and inside CharOption server function, do category() when you want to retrieve a value.

Think of it this way. When calling a module or function, passing category() means "pass the current value of category", while passing category means "pass the reactive expression itself", or alternatively, "pass all future values of category".

ui<-dashboardPage(
    dashboardHeader(),
    dashboardSidebar(disable = TRUE),
    dashboardBody(
    downloadButton('down','click me'),
    plotOutput('ab')

    ))

server<-function(input,output){
sample<-reactive({plot(iris)})

output$ab<-renderPlot(sample())

 output$down<- downloadHandler(
     'FUB.png',
     content = function(file){
        png(file)
        print(sample())
        dev.off()
     }
     )

}

shinyApp(ui,server)

messages.subject: Re: Download png from interactive plots
messages.subject_clean: Download png from interactive plots
messages.body_plain:
When plot() runs, it writes a png to disk; it does not return an object that can be printed (which is what you're trying to do). In more technical terms, the png is written as a side effect of running plot().

It happens that renderPlot will capture that png file and send it to the browser. However, when you try to run sample() again in your downloadHandler, it will not write a png to disk.

If you use ggplot() instead of plot(), it does return a printable object, so that would work. Another possibility is to move the plotting code out to a function, and call it from both the renderPlot() and from the downloadHandler callback. You would want to write the function so that any input values would be passed to it, as in myPlot(input$x, input$y).

-Winston

Right now I just have the same plotting code in both renderPlot and downloadHandler (the simulation is being done in an observeEvent once the data are submitted). The problem is that all of that code seems to be re-run when I hit "download", which means that I sometimes end up with a different plot downloaded than what's displayed (because of the randomness in the simulation).

How can ensure that the same plot gets downloaded that's being displayed?

messages.subject: Re: R Shiny server connect with Database
messages.subject_clean: R Shiny server connect with Database
messages.body_plain:
Depends on your choice of database, but you should be able to connect to the database with shiny in the exact same way you would when doing analyses in R.

You'll have to manage the database separately.

As far as anonymizing data, that is somewhat vague.

You'd want to make sure that:

1.  Your database and R's connection to it is secure.
2.  You use HTTPS to send and receive data.  This will require you deploying shiny server behind a SSL certificate.  Or using shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>, which uses TLS by default.
3.  If needed, you may want your DB to be encrypted at rest.

The last step is more complicated as it requires knowledge beyond R/Shiny to make sure everything works.

Erik

If you have a small budget and are new to databases and privacy is important I'd recommend something like:

AWS RDS w/ encryption at rest turned on.
In same VPC, host a small EC2 isntance w/ your shiny app.

messages.subject: Re: RShiny Crashes when i try to switch between SQL Database Server
messages.subject_clean: RShiny Crashes when i try to switch between SQL Database Server
messages.body_plain:
Without a runnable MRE, it's hard to tell the particular reason why your app is failing. What I can tell you, however, is that you should never be opening connections inside reactive blocks and not closing them -- it's possible that's what is causing the crash. On the other hand, it seems like you are using the RODBC package, which has some known issues.. Have you looked into the recent odbc package <http://db.rstudio.com/odbc/>? I think you'd be much better off with that. It's also DBI compliant, which means that in addition to having access to the very well maintained DBI interface, you can also use the dplyr and pool packages to create robust code that interacts efficiently with databases. The dplyr package translates dplyr code to SQL to allow you to query a database in a friendlier language and the pool package does connection management for you (i.e. if you follow best practices, you won't have to worry about closing connections, which is a likely cause for the problem you're experiencing now). If your app is large, this may mean that you have to invest some time upfront to migrate everything, but I'd strongly advice you to do that anyway.

If this sounds interesting to you, in addition to the link above, you should check out the following three articles (in this order):
Database basics - dplyr and DBI <https://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/overview.html>
Using the pool package (basics) <https://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/pool-basics.html>
Using dplyr and pool to query a database <http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/pool-dplyr.html>

Hello Barbara,

Thanks again for your thoughtful assistance. I think, in fact, that your method does work - I think the problem is with my javascript. I am attempting to use *.length to determine the number of records in the database but the more I play with it the less sure that I am returning what I expect. This app is intertwined with a massive postgres database so producing a reproducible example would be very challenging. However, I have included a bit more of the relevant code below with comments and wonder if you might suggest how I should be determining the number of records that I might pass into my conditional panel to use with your earlier suggestion? In fact, is there a way to view the value of output.sampleList.length (I am new to javascript)?

Thank you,
Stevan

ui

# the conditional panel per your earlier suggestion

column(10,
       conditionalPanel("output.sampleList.length >= 1",
                        dataTableUI("one")
       ),
       conditionalPanel("output.sampleList.length >= 2",
                        dataTableUI("two")
       ),
       conditionalPanel("output.sampleList.length >= 3",
                        dataTableUI("three")
       )
)

server <- function(input, output) {

# query sweepnet sample data for selected site

# safe to ignore all the sql, the important point is that it is returning a
# dataframe with one column (sweepnet_sample_id), and 0 to 3 rows depending on
# the number of records that are present in the database

sweepnetSamples <- reactive({

  # add listener for adding a sweepnet sample
  ssadd$sampleAdded

  pg_local <- databaseConn()

  baseSweepnetSamplesQuery <- "
      SELECT
      --  se.survey_id,
        ss.sweepnet_sample_id
      FROM survey200.sweepnet_samples ss
      JOIN survey200.sampling_events se ON (ss.survey_id = se.survey_id)
      JOIN survey200.sites sites ON (sites.site_id = se.site_id)
      WHERE
        EXTRACT (YEAR FROM se.samp_date) = ?year AND
        sites.site_code LIKE ?selectedSite
      ORDER BY ss.sweepnet_sample_id ASC;"

  sweepnetSamplesQuery <- sqlInterpolate(ANSI(),
                                         baseSweepnetSamplesQuery,
                                         year = surveyYear,
                                         selectedSite = input$s200site)
  sweepnetSampleIds <- dbGetQuery(pg_local, sweepnetSamplesQuery)

  dbDisconnect(pg_local)

  return(sweepnetSampleIds)

})

# create a vector (from 0 to 3) of records returned by the SQL query in
# sweepnetSamples() to pass as a list of samples for review by the user in the
# UI, and to use in conditional panels

output$sampleList <- reactive({

  sweepnetSamples()[,'sweepnet_sample_id']

})

# do not suspend hidden values

outputOptions(output, "sampleList", suspendWhenHidden = FALSE)

output$sampleList <- reactive({

column(10,

  ),
  conditionalPanel("output.sampleList >= 2",
    dataTableUI("two")
  ),
  conditionalPanel("output.sampleList >= 3",

  )

messages.subject: Using leafletProxy to make changes in layers and styles
messages.subject_clean: Using leafletProxy to make changes in layers and styles
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I'm making my first shiny app using leaflet and would like to get some advice on how to use the leafletProxy function correctly/efficiently to make changes in the map. In summary, I'm loading a large SpatialPolygonsDataFrame (a few thousand polygons) the first time I call leaflet in the server. Based on user inputs, the app should (1) apply a different style to a specific group of polygons (e.g. to countries of a particular continent), or (2) hide a specific polygon (e.g., the limit of a country) and display a more detailed SPDF with multiple polygons in its place (e.g., the states of that country).

For (1), my plan is to break the initial SPDF by groups (e.g. continents) and addPolygons() with a loop, defining a different name for each group using the "group" parameter. For changing the style of the polygons of a given group (e.g. change the fill color based on an attribute in its data frame), I could hide the original group using hideGroup() and add that same group with addPolygons(), but using the modified style. When that group is deselected by the user, I can clear the modified version with clearGroup() and show the original version again using showGroup(). Is this a good approach? Or is there a better/faster way of changing the style of a particular group of polygons?

For (2), the idea is the same. But in addition to specifying a "group" when I first add the polygons, looks like I'd need to specify a "layerId" for each polygon in that group in order to be able to remove any single polygon later using removeShape(). When that option for "showing the states of the country" is deselected, I could remove the new SPDF with clearGroup() and get the original polygon (the country limit) back in using addPolygons, specifying the original "group". I wonder if there is an equivalent of showGroup/hideGroup for showing/hiding a specific layerID. If so, I'm guessing that would be faster than removing/adding polygons every time.

Sorry for the long post and for not providing a reproducible example. I guess this is more of a conceptual question for understanding the best way of dealing with multiple layers in the context of leaflet/shiny... but I'd be happy to come up with a simple example if needed.

Many thanks,
Fabio

messages.subject_clean: Using leafletProxy to make changes in layers and styles
messages.body_plain:
Yes, those both sound fine. Although depending on the opacity of your restyled/detailed polygons for both (1) and (2), you might not need to hide the original polygons at all--just let them be covered by the new polygon, since it'll be the same shape.

On Fri, Aug 11, 2017 at 5:08 PM Fabio <fa...@canopyrss.tech> wrote:

> Hi,
>
> I'm making my first shiny app using leaflet and would like to get some advice on how to use the leafletProxy function correctly/efficiently to make changes in the map. In summary, I'm loading a large SpatialPolygonsDataFrame (a few thousand polygons) the first time I call leaflet in the server. Based on user inputs, the app should (1) apply a different style to a specific group of polygons (e.g. to countries of a particular continent), or (2) hide a specific polygon (e.g., the limit of a country) and display a more detailed SPDF with multiple polygons in its place (e.g., the states of that country).
>
> For (1), my plan is to break the initial SPDF by groups (e.g. continents) and addPolygons() with a loop, defining a different name for each group using the "group" parameter. For changing the style of the polygons of a given group (e.g. change the fill color based on an attribute in its data frame), I could hide the original group using hideGroup() and add that same group with addPolygons(), but using the modified style. When that group is deselected by the user, I can clear the modified version with clearGroup() and show the original version again using showGroup(). Is this a good approach? Or is there a better/faster way of changing the style of a particular group of polygons?
>
> For (2), the idea is the same. But in addition to specifying a "group" when I first add the polygons, looks like I'd need to specify a "layerId" for each polygon in that group in order to be able to remove any single polygon later using removeShape(). When that option for "showing the states of the country" is deselected, I could remove the new SPDF with clearGroup() and get the original polygon (the country limit) back in using addPolygons, specifying the original "group". I wonder if there is an equivalent of showGroup/hideGroup for showing/hiding a specific layerID. If so, I'm guessing that would be faster than removing/adding polygons every time.
>
> Sorry for the long post and for not providing a reproducible example. I guess this is more of a conceptual question for understanding the best way of dealing with multiple layers in the context of leaflet/shiny... but I'd be happy to come up with a simple example if needed.
>
> Many thanks,
> Fabio
>

messages.subject: Re: Build radio buttons by raw HTML, how can I get the input of these buttons?
messages.subject_clean: Build radio buttons by raw HTML, how can I get the input of these buttons?
messages.body_plain:
You can only access the "input" object from inside of a server function. If you want to separate the code for the observer out into a separate file, that's fine, but you have to create a function that creates the observer, then call that function from within the server function. The reason for this is that each input object belongs to a specific browser session, and the server function is invoked for each session as it starts up; so if you just try to access input from outside the server function, we don't know which input object you mean.

Also, I don't think that HTML will work unless you also wrap it in <div id="your_input_id", class="shiny-input-radiogroup">, and you can drop the "id" attribute from the individual radio buttons as you'll just use input$your_input_id to access the value.

messages.subject: Turning off popovers
messages.subject_clean: Turning off popovers
messages.body_plain:
This should be a goal of fairly wide interest; Implement popovers (or tooltips), and a toggle allowing user so turn them off, and on again, at will. Works in a way, but in curious fashion. My project is at github.com/professorbeautiful/DUE and viewable at trials.shinyapps.io/DUEshiny The popovers are implemented in a function addAllPopovers() beginning with cat("addAllPopovers\n") with 19 commands like addPopover(session, 'popFavoriteDose', title="Dose", content="Select a dose by clicking on plot (left),
or type or scroll here.") The code to turn them all off is: > stopAllPopovers = function(){ > cat("stopAllPopovers\n") > output$JSevaluation = renderUI({ > scriptString = paste( > 'stopAllPopoversString = > "$(\\"*[id^=\\\'pop\\\']\\").popover(\\\'destroy\\\');" ;', > 'eval(stopAllPopoversString); ' > ) > tags$script( scriptString ) > } ) > } Works great. The javascript created is > stopAllPopoversString = > "$(\"*[id^=\'pop\']\").popover(\'destroy\');" ; eval(stopAllPopoversString); And by golly, in a JS console it works. And, stopAllPopovers works... in a fashion. So with a checkbox for toggle, we have > observeEvent(input$togglePopovers, { > cat('input$togglePopovers a', input$togglePopovers, '\n') > if(input$togglePopovers) > addAllPopovers() > else > stopAllPopovers() > }) Clicking the checkbox does indeed call the expected functions, like so: > input$togglePopovers FALSE > stopAllPopovers > input$togglePopovers TRUE > addAllPopovers > input$togglePopovers FALSE > stopAllPopovers > input$togglePopovers TRUE > addAllPopovers Etc. So what's wrong? 1) It takes TWO clicks on the toggle to turn on, or turn off, the popovers. So sometimes stopAllPopovers enables the popovers, and sometimes addAllPopovers disables them! 2) Sometimes, upon restarting the program, not all the popovers are enabled. Then, after two clicks on the checkbox, the disabled ones are enabled, and the enabled and disabled. The division into two sets of popovers differs each time. By the way, the bottom of the app window has my shinyDebuggingPanel, which is super-useful for running either R or JS code inside the app. Toggle it open, and away you go. For example, you can test addAllPopovers(), stopAllPopovers() directly.

#   for non-clicked bars
#

library(shiny)

# Create dataframe
df = data.frame(x = c("A", "A", "B", "B", "C", "C"), y = c(1/2, 1/2, 1/3, 2/3, 1/4, 3/4), z = c("X", "Y", "X", "Y", "X", "Y"))

ui = fluidPage(
    headerPanel("Test Multiple Selection Bar Plot"),
    plotOutput("plot1", click = "plot1_click"),
    br(),
    br(),
    br(),
    verbatimTextOutput("testdf")
)

server = function(input, output) {

    # rv is the reactive value to store cumulatively the clicked bars in bar graph
    rv = reactiveValues(clickgrp = NULL)

    # get the dataframe based on selected bars in bargraph
    getdf = eventReactive(input$plot1_click$x, {

        rv$clickgrp = c(rv$clickgrp, input$plot1_click$x)
        keeprows <- as.numeric(df$x) %in% round(rv$clickgrp)
        df2 = df[keeprows, ]
        df2c = df[!keeprows, ]

        list(df2 = df2, df2c = df2c)

    # bar plot
    output$plot1 = renderPlot({

        if(!is.null(input$plot1_click$x)) {
            df2 = getdf()$df2

        } else {

    output$testdf = renderPrint({

messages.body_plain:
Never mind, I found out my mistake. The ShinyDevCon video by Winston Change helped where he talks about adding points to a graph. The link to the video is:
https://www.rstudio.com/resources/videos/coordinated-multiple-views-linked-brushing/
He specifically talks about the adding of points to a graph around 13 min. I modified the above code accordingly and have put the version of code below which works fine.

#
#   Goal: In a bar graph, I want to click multiple bars and get the data for that and also highlight just the clicked bars by increasing transparency
#   for non-clicked bars
#

library(shiny)
library(ggplot2)

# Create dataframe
df = data.frame(x = c("A", "A", "B", "B", "C", "C"), y = c(1/2, 1/2, 1/3, 2/3, 1/4, 3/4), z = c("X", "Y", "X", "Y", "X", "Y"))

# ui
ui = fluidPage(
  headerPanel("Test Multiple Selection Bar Plot"),
  plotOutput("plot1", click = "plot1_click"),
  br(),
  br(),

  actionButton("clearfilter", "Clear Filters"),

  br(),
  br(),
  br(),
  verbatimTextOutput("testdf")
)

# server
server = function(input, output) {

  # rv is the reactive value to store cumulatively the clicked bars in bar graph

  rv = reactiveValues(clickgrp = NULL, dfr = df, dfrc = NULL)

  # get the dataframe based on selected bars in bargraph

  observeEvent(input$plot1_click$x, {

    rv$clickgrp = c(rv$clickgrp, input$plot1_click$x)
    keeprows <- as.numeric(df$x) %in% round(rv$clickgrp)

    rv$dfr = df[keeprows, ]
    rv$dfrc = df[!keeprows, ]

  })

  observeEvent(input$clearfilter, {

    rv$clickgrp = NULL
    rv$dfr = df
    rv$dfrc = NULL

  })

  # bar plot
  output$plot1 = renderPlot({

      df2 = rv$dfr
      df2c = rv$dfrc

    p = ggplot() + geom_bar(data = df2, aes(x = x, y = y, fill = z), stat = "identity")
    if(!is.null(df2c)) {
      p = p + geom_bar(data = df2c, aes(x = x, y = y, fill = z), alpha = 0.3, stat = "identity")
    }
    p = p + scale_fill_discrete(drop = FALSE) + theme_bw()
    p
  })

  output$testdf = renderPrint({

    rv$dfr
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)

messages.body_plain:
I think you're encountering this issue, where a https resource won't load properly in the RStudio viewer in Windows.
  https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/issues/1148

Even though you're using a http URL, the image from wikimedia.org <http://wikimedia.org> gets redirected to a https URL.

If you open it in a regular web browser, it will show properly.

The issue has been filed with the RStudio IDE team.

-Winston

library(shiny)
library(shinydashboard)

#OBJECTIVE HTML

#TREATMENT MODELS TABLE
output$Table1 <- DT::renderDataTable({
  DT::datatable(options = list(paging = FALSE, searching= TRUE,
                               autoWidth = TRUE, ordering=FALSE,
                               columnDefs = list(list(width = '800px', targets = "_all"))),
                Treatment_Models[,]
  )
})

})

messages.body_plain:
Hi

I have a shiny dashboard app that shows a DT datatable.  The raw data is manipulated in a function based on user inputs on the sidebar.  All is good and working well.

My question is how do I get the data table to render in an Rmarkdown html page.  Nothing I've tried works.

Here is a simple code by way of an example.  I wish the table to render in an Rmarkdown page when I click a download button.

library(shiny)
library(DT)
data(iris)

ui <- fluidPage(

   titlePanel("|Species Table"),

   sidebarLayout(
      sidebarPanel(
         selectInput("specs",
                     "Number of bins:",
                     unique(iris$Species))
      ),

      # Show a plot of the generated distribution
      mainPanel(
         tableOutput("specTable")
      )
   )
)

server <- function(input, output) {

  subSpec <- function(x){
    iris[iris$Species == x, -5]
    iris[1:10,]
  }

  reactiveFunction <- reactive({ subSpec(input$specs) })

  output$reactiveTable <- renderDataTable({ reactiveFunction() }, rownames = FALSE)

  output$specTable <- renderUI({

messages.body_plain:
This error:

Error: Unable to retrieve package records for the following packages:
- "JM"

usually means you've installed a package in a way that rsconnect (actually packrat) can't tell where it came from. Most commonly, it means you ran R CMD INSTALL locally (or equivalent, like Build in an RStudio package project). You can fix this by installing using install.packages or devtools::install_github, and deploying again.

messages.subject: Re: Shiny DT datatable to rmarkdown
messages.subject_clean: Shiny DT datatable to rmarkdown
messages.body_plain:
See the Parameterized Reports feature. If you define, say, a "data" parameter in the yaml header, then when calling rmarkdown::render you can pass params=list(data=reactiveFunction()), and then in your Rmd you can refer to params$data to fetch that data and wrap it in a DT or whatever.

messages.subject: Passing a student ID from Moodle to a Shiny App
messages.subject_clean: Passing a student ID from Moodle to a Shiny App
messages.body_plain:
Hi All,

I’m working with a grad student to create a Shiny Dashboard that will give individual students a visual way to track their progress in a course – sort of using analytics to help learn analytics.

We want a student to be able to run the app as an LTI link from the Moodle LMS, and pass the student’s ID to the app in a secure way.

I’m already telling you more than I know—before I go venture into the mysteries of LTI, PHP and other foreign lands, does anyone have experience or code snippets that would allow our Shiny app to generate keys and secrets?

Thanks for any help you can offer. And to be clear, my Shiny skills are OK, but I have no PHP background (as I understand it, Moodle is written in PHP) and I have the most rudimentary knowledge re: LTI.

Feeling my limits,

Rob
